newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP may buy PT Krakatau Steel stake-paper.
newsitem.headline: BHP may buy PT Krakatau Steel stake-paper.

text.p: Australia's largest company and only significant steel producer, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, may buy a stake in PT Krakatau Steel which was now owned by the Indonesian government, The Australian newspaper said in a front-page report on Tuesday.

The newspaper said Melbourne-based BHP, which recently announced a winding back of local steel production with the planned closure of the Newcastle operation in 1999, had confirmed that it was talking to PT Krakatau about a possible investment.
"We are having a look at it (Krakatau)," BHP Indonesia president Colin Smith said.
"We have had some discussions in relation to the IPO (initial public offering) but we do not have any agreement to take a stake," Smith said.
The newspaper said the sale of Krakatau was expected to raise US$650 million for the Indonesian government.
It said BHP Steel had denied a report in Indonesia that it may take a 25 percent stake ahead of the public offering in October. The paper did not identify the source of the report.
BHP Steel and Krakatau Steel have a metallic and paint line joint venture in Indonesia while Krakatau is a major customer of BHP's steel and mineral products, the paper said.

Indonesian Trade and Industry Minister Tunky Ariwibowo personally approached BHP Steel chief Ron McNeilly in March to consider taking a stake in Krakatau but at the time BHP played down any chance of an investment, it said.
